clue.text: (& 25ac.) Catchy, so composition leads to easy intercourse

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters before it are arranged afresh

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A catchy tune leads, by way of romance, to easy-going sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye plays on 'intercourse' meaning sex; here it is used in its old sense of conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Intercourse in its older sense is conversation, and a relaxed, friendly conversation is a comfortable little talk.

clue.text: Cameron's opening shot possibly backfiring – cause for pause

blocks.note: the first letter of the former Prime Minister's name
shot is one example of ammunition, shortened to ammo

explanation.surface: David Cameron's first shot goes off in his face, which ought to make him stop and think.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark of this kind makes a reader take a short pause, so it is something that causes one.

clue.text: Tory leader in decline – flop, schoolboy joke

clue.text: Holds up sexy picture for the cops?

explanation.walkthrough: The mugging and the police photograph fit together, so the surface is nearly a story about a robber caught on camera.
explanation.definitionFit: Police take a face photograph of every person they arrest, filed for identification.

clue.text: ERM in England? You devised dodgy means of cleaning up

blocks.note: all fifteen letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Britain's Exchange Rate Mechanism was a crooked scheme to clean up financially.
explanation.walkthrough: The ERM is the Exchange Rate Mechanism, which Britain left on Black Wednesday in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing criminal profits through legitimate businesses makes dirty cash look clean, an illegal way of tidying up money.

clue.text: Male presidential candidate regularly in a state

explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up and agitated is the idiomatic sense of being in a state.

clue.text: Shag upper class-style, on the wagon – and get rid of any damp patch

clue.text: British old crock, a stirrer

explanation.definitionFit: Making beer involves stirring the mash, and a person who brews up trouble also stirs it.

clue.text: The bane of UKIP? Cyclops is, one way and another, and possibly Hugh is

explanation.surface: Cyclops and Hugh Grant are both, in their ways, what UKIP most hates.
explanation.walkthrough: UKIP was the UK Independence Party, campaigning against immigration; I'M is written forwards and then backwards before Hugh Grant's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: UKIP's chief campaigning target was people arriving to settle in Britain from abroad.
